subject: Elementary School Overcrowding and Potential Redistricting
overview: The committee approved over $285,000 in grants and discussed urgent operational challenges, including severe overcrowding at Roberts Elementary and ongoing school bus driver shortages.

items.title: Consent Agenda and Minutes
items.summary: Approved bills, payrolls, and meeting minutes from June, July, and August with an amendment to the June 24 minutes regarding a vote tally.

items.title: Grant Approvals
items.summary: Approved a $35,000 Cummings Foundation grant for the Center for Citizenship and Social Responsibility, a $50,000 Music Drives Us grant for Roberts Elementary music equipment, and a $200,000 Bar Foundation grant for high school instructional vision.

items.title: Culinary Arts Field Trip
items.summary: Approved an out-of-state field trip for 23 culinary arts students to visit Johnson and Wales University in Rhode Island.

items.title: Summer Programming Report
items.summary: Staff presented data on summer initiatives including special education services, English Learner enrichment, high school credit recovery, and a new literacy acceleration academy.

items.title: Enrollment and Personnel Updates
items.summary: The committee reviewed preliminary enrollment figures highlighting significant disparities between elementary schools, noting that several teaching and paraprofessional positions remain vacant.

items.title: Roberts Elementary Overcrowding and Redistricting
items.summary: Teachers and committee members discussed the capacity crisis at Roberts Elementary, where enrollment has surpassed 590 students, prompting a call for redistricting and strategic planning this fall.

items.title: Brooks School Boiler and Capital Purchases
items.summary: Approved the purchase of a natural gas condensing hot water heater for the Brooks School because full electrification was deemed too expensive and would require major electrical infrastructure upgrades.

items.title: Transportation and Bus Shortages
items.summary: The district reported that contractor Eastern Bus is currently unable to provide four of eighteen contracted buses due to a driver shortage, causing overcrowding and potential eligibility changes on middle school routes.

items.title: Facilities, Food Service, and Technology
items.summary: Updates included the completion of lighting upgrades, bathroom facelifts at the high school, and the purchase of 950 Chromebooks and new kitchen equipment.

items.title: Policy Updates
items.summary: Approved the first reading of a revised non-discrimination policy to align with new Title IX regulations and amended the consent agenda policy to include recurring grant and field trip approvals.
